title: Uniracers
subtitle: One wheel, no rider
summary: Uniracers is DMA Design’s unusual Super Nintendo racing game about unicycles that need nobody to ride them. body: Uniracers is DMA Design’s unusual Super Nintendo racing game about unicycles that need nobody to ride them. Released in Europe as Unirally, it sends the animated machines along two-dimensional tracks filled with loops, jumps and abrupt changes of direction. Performing a stunt increases speed, so acrobatics are part of racing well rather than an optional flourish. The player must turn a brief moment in the air into an advantage and still land safely enough to carry that extra pace into the next section.

Stunts involve jumping and rotating around different axes. Completing one cleanly rewards the unicycle with speed, while landing badly causes a crash and loses the momentum already earned. The decision is therefore about how much can fit into the available space. A generous jump permits a longer combination; a low or crowded section demands restraint. Track markings provide information about what lies ahead, including shortcuts and hazards. Learning those visual signals helps the player prepare a stunt before the unicycle reaches the next take-off.

The forty-five tracks are grouped into nine tours, with races, circuits and stunt events giving the same controls different objectives. Two-player split-screen play supports direct competition, and a league mode can organise several people into one-on-one races. The unicycles can also be named and retain individual progress. Those features give the small cast of differently coloured machines a social identity without introducing riders. Uniracers builds its personality from their movement: a good run looks playful because every successful trick is also useful to the race.
